claim: A null key on a positional record property is silently ignored instead of producing MsgPack005. A positional record property is declared by a ParameterSyntax, not a PropertyDeclarationSyntax, so GetPropertyIdentifierLocation returns null even though the property is declared in the current source. ReportIfLocatedInCompilation then discards the resulting diagnostic. For example, `[MessagePackObject] public partial record R([property: Key(null)] string Value);` receives no BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull diagnostic.

receipt_plan.detail: Add NullKeyOnPositionalRecordPropertyReportsMsgPack005, which runs the generator and all MessagePack analyzers on a source-declared partial record whose positional property has [property: Key(null)] and expects MsgPack005 on the Value identifier. On head, the diagnostic is absent because the helper cannot obtain a location from ParameterSyntax.

claim: Only two of the three unguarded DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0] diagnostic paths identified in the requirement are changed. The remaining path at the reporter's TypeCollector.cs:735 can still evaluate the indexer before reportDiagnostic is invoked; the new ReportIfLocatedInCompilation wrapper runs too late to prevent that exception. Thus a metadata symbol that reaches this third diagnostic can still crash the analyzer or generator, contrary to the criterion that diagnostics requiring a source location must not crash for symbols without declaring syntax.

receipt_plan.detail: Inspect the remaining DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0] access at the reporter-identified third diagnostic path (TypeCollector.cs:735 in the issue revision).
